posts.title: Route 66 on the Way to Kansas City
posts.meta_description: Our Route 66 drives from Texas to Kansas City in 2013 and 2023: the Golden Driller, Blue Whale of Catoosa, Baxter Springs, Rainbow Bridge and OKKAMO marker.
posts.body:
Some trips are about the destination. These were supposed to be. Asia and I have driven from Texas to Kansas City twice, in January 2013 and again in January 2023, and somewhere along the way we decided the fastest road wasn't the most interesting one. So we got off the highway and onto old Route 66, and I'm really glad we did.

Route 66 turned 100 this year, and you can feel that age in the best way. The towns are smaller, the signs are hand-painted, and every few miles somebody has built something big and a little crazy just to make you pull over. We pulled over a lot.

## Which Route 66 stops did we make on the way to Kansas City?

Asia and I stopped at the Golden Driller, the Blue Whale of Catoosa, and Ed Galloway's Totem Pole Park near Foyil. Next came Baxter Springs, the Rainbow Bridge just north of it, and the OKKAMO tri-state marker near Joplin, where Oklahoma, Kansas and Missouri meet.

## The Golden Driller

Our first big stop was the Golden Driller in Tulsa, Oklahoma. He's a giant statue of an oil worker, and he looks every bit the part of Oklahoma's oil country. We took photos with Asia in front of him, and he really is huge.

## The Blue Whale of Catoosa

Next came the Blue Whale of Catoosa. It's a big, smiling blue whale sitting at the edge of a pond, right off Route 66. We walked inside and all around it, and we took plenty of photos.

## Ed Galloway's Totem Pole Park

After the whale we found the totem poles at Ed Galloway's Totem Pole Park, just off Route 66 in Foyil, Oklahoma. These are tall, brightly painted concrete totems, hand-built a long time ago and still standing out there in the Oklahoma countryside.

## Baxter Springs

Crossing into Kansas, our first stop was Baxter Springs, a small Route 66 town. We stopped at the Route 66 visitor information center there and took more photos.

## Rainbow Bridge

Just north of Baxter Springs, we stopped at the Rainbow Bridge. It's an old white arched bridge from the early days of the highway, and it's a well-known stop on this stretch of Route 66. Kansas only has a short piece of the old road, about 13 miles, but it makes every mile count. We walked out on it and took a photo there too.

## The OKKAMO Tri-State Marker

One of the stops was the OKKAMO Tri-State Marker near Joplin, where Oklahoma, Kansas and Missouri meet. It's close to Route 66, and you can stand in all three states at once.

## Just Driving the Road

In between all the named stops was the best part, which was just driving it. Old Route 66 winds through small towns, past old gas stations and faded signs, and it gives you time to look around instead of just getting somewhere. If you're making a drive like this, give yourself a few extra hours. You'll want them.

## Kansas City: The Majestic and Hotel Phillips

When we finally rolled into Kansas City, we ate at [the Majestic](https://totinmypack.com/restaurants.html#restaurant-the-majestic-restaurant-kansas-city), and I had the steak. The piano player was amazing.

We stayed at [Hotel Phillips Kansas City](https://totinmypack.com/hotels.html#hotel-hotel-phillips-kansas-city), part of Hilton's Curio Collection. We love the art deco style, and the rooms are great. It's our go-to place to stay in Kansas City.

## Our Travel Films

You can find all our travel films, from Greece to the back roads of the United States, on our [Films page](https://totinmypack.com/videos.html) and on our YouTube channel at [youtube.com/@TotinMyPack](https://www.youtube.com/@TotinMyPack). More Route 66 stops, gathered from more than one trip, are on our [Route 66 trip page](https://totinmypack.com/trips/route-66.html), and the films are collected under [Route 66](https://totinmypack.com/destinations/route-66.html).

If you've driven Route 66, I'd love to hear your favorite stop. And if you haven't, take the old road next time. Pull over for the whale. You won't regret it.

posts.title: Our 2024 Virginia Road Trip: The Coast, Roanoke and Walton's Mountain
posts.meta_description: Our November 2024 Virginia road trip: Norfolk, Virginia Beach, Cape Charles, Appomattox, Roanoke, New River Gorge, Walton's Mountain and Monticello.
posts.body:
Asia and I were on Virginia Beach at sunrise when we saw a proposal out on the sand. The sun was coming up over the water, and a couple was out there on the beach. Asia filmed it, and she was able to share her video with the couple afterward. It moved her, and of everything on this trip, that's the moment she loved most.

In November 2024, we flew from Dallas to Norfolk. We started on the Virginia coast, then drove west, with a stop at New River Gorge in West Virginia, and through some of Virginia's history, including Walton's Mountain in Schuyler.

Here's how the trip went, in the order we drove it.

## Norfolk and Virginia Beach

We landed in Norfolk and stayed at [Hilton Norfolk The Main](https://totinmypack.com/hotels.html#hotel-hilton-norfolk-the-main-norfolk), a modern 23-story hotel at the corner of Main and Granby Streets, right on the downtown waterfront, overlooking the Elizabeth River. From our room we looked out over the river and the city skyline. In the evening the lights came on across the water, and that same view was waiting when we came back to the window later. The staff were warm and welcoming from the moment we checked in.

Our first dinner was at Rockafeller's in Virginia Beach, looking out over Rudee Inlet. Asia had oysters with mignonette, and I had pork ribs. The next morning we were back on the beach for sunrise, and that's when we saw the proposal. Afterward we sat down to breakfast at Pocahontas Pancake & Waffle House.

## Cape Charles and the Chrysler Museum

From there we crossed the Chesapeake Bay Bridge-Tunnel to Cape Charles, a long run of bridges and tunnels with the water on either side. We walked around the historic downtown and along the waterfront, and we ate at The Oyster Farm. Asia had oysters again, and I had a cheeseburger that was one of the best I've ever had. We watched sailboats out on the bay while we were there.

Back in Norfolk, we went to the Chrysler Museum of Art. Admission was free. We spent time inside among the galleries, and Asia fell in love with the glass collection, including work by Chihuly and Tiffany.

This part of the trip is in our film [Norfolk, Virginia Beach & Cape Charles](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jNoREzI7-B0).

## Suffolk and Appomattox

From the coast we headed west and stopped in Suffolk, where we had some peanut snacks and spent a little time downtown. Then we went on to Appomattox Court House National Historical Park. The park is a cluster of old buildings set among open fields, and we saw the McLean House there.

## Roanoke and New River Gorge

In Roanoke we stayed at [The Hotel Roanoke & Conference Center](https://totinmypack.com/hotels.html#hotel-hotel-roanoke-roanoke), a Tudor-style hotel near downtown, in Virginia's Blue Ridge. It was built in 1882 as the railroad hotel at the heart of the growing town, and it has been taking in guests for more than a century. It's on the National Register of Historic Places, and it's part of Hilton's Curio Collection. The hotel closed in 1989 and reopened in 1995 after a restoration. The distinctive Tudor exterior is hard to miss. Inside, you come first into a lobby filled with antiques, where the original Czech-made chandeliers still hang, along with the woodwork and the old elevator doors. The staff here were warm and welcoming too, and that made the old place feel like home.

We also crossed into West Virginia to visit New River Gorge National Park, including the New River Gorge Bridge. From the overlooks we looked down at the river and out at the long steel arch spanning the gorge.

Back in Roanoke, we visited the Basilica of Saint Andrew, with its stained glass, and the Norfolk & Western Historical Society, where we looked at the exhibits, including a train model. Then we went up to the Roanoke Star, on the mountain above town, with the city spread out below and the star standing among the trees.

This part of the trip is in our film [Appomattox, Roanoke & New River Gorge](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y0EhqN3QnnY).

## Schuyler, Monticello and Lynchburg

We visited Schuyler, the hometown of Earl Hamner Jr., who created The Waltons, and the real-life inspiration for Walton's Mountain. We went to Walton's Mountain Museum and saw his printing press, and we also visited the Walton Hamner House.

In Lynchburg we stayed at [The Virginian Hotel](https://totinmypack.com/hotels.html#hotel-the-virginian-hotel-lynchburg), on Church Street downtown. It opened in 1913 as a five-story Beaux-Arts hotel, designed by Verus T. Ritter, and after a complete renovation it reopened in 2018 as part of Hilton's Curio Collection. It's a historic, restored landmark, and you see that as soon as you come in: arched windows, an ornate lobby with 30-foot barrel-vaulted ceilings and curved skylights, and grand marble stairs with wrought iron railings. After dark, we looked out from the hotel over the street and the buildings downtown. And like the other two hotels on this trip, the staff were warm and welcoming.

From there we went to Thomas Jefferson's Poplar Forest, and then to Lexington, where we visited Lee Chapel, walked the grounds at Washington & Lee University, and passed under the arch at Virginia Military Institute. We also went to Monticello and to Michie Tavern, which dates to around 1784, and we ate there. We visited James Monroe's Highland, walked around Lynchburg, and stopped at Liberty University, including DeMoss Hall and the School of Business.

This part of the trip is in our film [From The Waltons to Monticello](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=S_K-LyRann0).

## Our Travel Films

You can find all our travel films, from Greece to the back roads of the United States, on our [Films page](https://totinmypack.com/videos.html) and on our YouTube channel at [youtube.com/@TotinMyPack](https://www.youtube.com/@TotinMyPack). The three films from this trip are [Norfolk, Virginia Beach & Cape Charles](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=jNoREzI7-B0), [Appomattox, Roanoke & New River Gorge](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=y0EhqN3QnnY), and [From The Waltons to Monticello](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=S_K-LyRann0). They're gathered on our [Virginia 2024 trip page](https://totinmypack.com/trips/virginia-2024.html) and under [Southeast & Mid-Atlantic](https://totinmypack.com/destinations/southeast.html). A shorter look at Schuyler is in [Walton's Mountain](https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=G5kivYsHDZ8) on TeddyUnscripted.
